133.0.0.en: Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together!

133.0.1.en: 1- The best thing in the relationship between people is for brethren to dwell together; what is meant is not dwelling in houses, but spiritual dwelling, that is, unity in worship, so that they worship God with one heart. This used to happen in the temple, as the priests and Levites chanted this psalm when they entered for worship and the practice of their service. This was also the feeling of those returning from captivity to build the temple and restore the worship of God with one heart, since they had become one people and were no longer divided into a northern and a southern kingdom as they were before the captivity.

133.0.2.en: 2- For brethren to be able to gather and dwell together, each one must be purified from his sins, and believe in God and live with Him, and then he can love the brethren. Worship in unity is made easy in the Church of the New Testament when the Holy Spirit begets the believers from one womb, which is Baptism, and unites them in the sacrament of Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord, so that it becomes natural for them to worship God with one heart, as the Apostles continued in worship with one accord (Acts 1:14).

133.1.0.en: It is like the precious ointment upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, even Aaron's beard, that went down to the skirts of his garments.

133.1.1.en: 1- David likens the love of brethren for one another to the perfume, or oil, that Moses poured on the head of Aaron when he anointed him high priest. This oil ran down from the head and descended upon the beard, then ran from the beard to the neckline of the robe, and it was a beautiful sight.

133.1.2.en: 2- Aaron the high priest signifies Christ, the High Priest of our New Testament, and He is the head of the body upon whom His Holy Spirit is poured, and it runs down from Him to the beard, which signifies the Apostles; for the beard grows on the mature, the grown and the full-grown, and the beard signifies the Apostles because it is attached to the head, who is Christ. Then the oil runs from the beard to all His garments, even to their skirts. The garments signify the believers, and the skirts signify all the believers, and so they are all united through the pouring out of the Holy Spirit upon them.

133.1.3.en: 3- And the oil that runs down upon the beard comes from the head and carries the fragrance of the head, which belongs to Christ, so all the believers receive the sweet fragrance of Christ (2 Cor 2:15).

133.1.4.en: 4- The Holy Spirit used to be poured on certain persons in the Old Testament, such as the high priest, the prophet and the king, but in the New Testament He is given to all the believers and dwells in them permanently, and not temporarily as in the Old Testament. And for the Holy Spirit to work in the believers, constant repentance is needed and attachment to the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace.

133.2.0.en: As the dew of Hermon, and as the dew that descended upon the mountains of Zion; for there the LORD commanded the blessing, life for evermore.

133.2.1.en: 1- Mount Hermon is in eastern Lebanon, and its summit is high, rising 9,200 feet above sea level.

133.2.2.en: The summit of the mountain is covered with snow, and abundant dew flows from the summit and descends the mountain to the small hills adjoining it, such as the hill of Sion, or Zion, which is different from the hill of Zion on which Jerusalem in Judea was built. This dew makes forests and vineyards grow, and the dew tempers the air in the heat of summer.

133.2.3.en: 2- The dew of Hermon, descending abundantly on the mountain and the surrounding hills, signifies the pouring out of the Holy Spirit on the believers in the Church. And as the dew of Hermon gives life to the plants and trees, so it gives the believers spiritual growth, and fruits, which are the virtues.

133.2.4.en: 3- If the writer of the psalm likens the love of brethren to the dew of Hermon, which signifies the pouring out of the Holy Spirit on the Church, then all of these give a growing spiritual life to the believers, and extend with them for ever in the Kingdom of Heaven. For the love of brethren grants them a pure life with God, and overcomes all the devil's cunning of strife, or divisions, and by this love prepares them for the Kingdom of Heaven.

133.2.5.en: 4- As the dew of Hermon tempers the plants and trees growing on the mountain and at its foot, so also the love of brethren tempers the relationship between them, and supports them before trials, which are signified by the intense rays of the sun, and gives them a beautiful feeling that makes them happy in their life, and makes them grow in their love for God.

133.2.6.en: If Satan tries to disturb you with the mistakes and offenses of those around you, hasten to prayer with humility, and the Holy Spirit who dwells in you will give you calm, and even turn you from distress to pity for them, so that you pray for them.

133.2.7.en: The night prayer in the sanctuary. A song of ascents. “Behold, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD ...” v. 1. Introduction:

133.2.8.en: 1- Its writer: unknown; it is one of the orphan psalms, because the name of the writer is not in the title of the psalm.

133.2.9.en: 2- When was it written? Not known precisely, and it may be:

133.2.10.en: a- In the days of David, or Solomon, to encourage the priests and Levites and the believers to worship and praise God in His temple.

133.2.11.en: b- The days of Nehemiah, who took care to restore and organize the service in the temple of the Lord, and he encourages the priests and Levites to praise.

133.2.12.en: 3- This psalm is a call to the priests and Levites to offer the evening worship, which is the evening burnt offering, and the prayers and praises offered in the temple, and that is in (vv. 1, 2). And the high priest answers them in (v. 3) and gives them the blessing from the Lord. It is therefore a liturgical psalm offered by the company of the priests and Levites, and the believers.

133.2.13.en: 4- There is a relation between this psalm and the one before it, which tells us of the work of the Holy Spirit in the believers, while this psalm tells us of the final effect of the Holy Spirit, which is the love of praise and being with God.

133.2.14.en: 5- This psalm is offered and prayed on the last of the steps of the ascent to the temple of the Lord, which is the fifteenth step, where they reach the temple and enter it and offer prayers and praises.

133.2.15.en: 6- This psalm suits the believers at every time, and especially in the nights, to encourage them to prayer and praise.

133.2.16.en: 7- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Compline, and as the introduction to the prayer of Midnight, where it calls the worshipers to praise God and to enjoy being before Him after the preoccupations of the long day.

134.0.0.en: Behold, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD, who by night stand in the house of the LORD.

134.0.1.en: 1- The psalm addresses the servants of the Lord who love His house and stand before Him for prayer and praise and blessing the Lord, in the night when people are quiet and asleep. But the priests and Levites and the believers who love God offer the evening burnt offering, which expresses their love for God, since the whole sacrifice is burned to please Him, and the offering of the sacrifice is accompanied by prayers expressing their love for God. And prayer in the night declares that these worshipers loved God more than sleep and the rest of the body, so they spent part of the night in prayer because their hearts were attached to Him, like David who said, “At midnight I will rise to give thanks unto You because of Your righteous judgments” (Ps 119:62).

134.0.2.en: 2- If in the Old Testament a person had to be clean when entering the temple, then all the more in the New Testament a person must be penitent and pure in order to share in the prayers of the Church and her praises, whether in the Liturgies or the other prayers.

134.0.3.en: 3- Some people loved God and prayer and praise in His house, so that they lived their life night and day in praise, like Anna the daughter of Phanuel (Lk 2:36-37).

134.1.0.en: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary, and bless the LORD.

134.1.1.en: 1- Lifting the hands in prayer means:

134.1.2.en: a- Declaring repentance, and asking purity and forgiveness from God.

134.1.3.en: b- Supplication to God, and this means need and humility.

134.1.4.en: c- Faith in God to whom we lift our hands, for He is our Deliverer and our only support.

134.1.5.en: d- Joining prayer with the lifting of the hands means our readiness to act, and not only to speak, that is, we strive and do all we can to be rid of our sins and to acquire every virtue.

134.1.6.en: e- Lifting the hands means the sign of the Cross, as Moses lifted his hands, and the children of Israel prevailed over Amalek (Ex 17:11). So lifting the hands is holding fast to the Cross that gives us spiritual victory.

134.1.7.en: Therefore St. Paul the Apostle in the New Testament calls us to lift up holy hands before God in prayer (1 Tim 2:8).

134.1.8.en: 2- The believers used to pray lifting clean hands and looking toward the sanctuary of the tabernacle of meeting, or the temple of the Lord, that is, looking toward the holy place, as Daniel did (Dan 6:10), and as we pray toward the sanctuary which is in the east in the Church of the New Testament.

134.1.9.en: 3- Lifting the hands and looking toward the sanctuary is accompanied by blessing the Lord, that is, praise and thanksgiving for all that God has done with us all day long, or all our life.

134.2.0.en: The LORD bless you out of Zion, He who made heaven and earth.

134.2.1.en: 1- If the writer of the psalm is calling the priests and Levites and the believers to bless the Lord, they receive a blessing after this in (v. 3). And if the high priest is the one who calls to bless the Lord in (vv. 1, 2), they answer him in (v. 3). In sum, this psalm closes with a blessing that comes from the Lord to the worshipers standing in the sanctuary in the nights. And this blessing means:

134.2.2.en: a- The divine forgiveness and the purity granted by God to the priests.

134.2.3.en: b- Inner renewal and being filled with God.

134.2.4.en: c- The person himself becomes a blessing to those around him.

134.2.5.en: 2- The Law commanded Aaron and his sons the priests to bless the people who believe in God (Num 6:23-26).

134.2.6.en: 3- This blessing comes from God, the Maker of heaven and earth, that is, He in whose hand is everything, and He gives this blessing from Zion, that is, from His temple, or from the Church, or from heaven. It is a great blessing, indeed the highest gift in the world. This means that there is a special blessing in the Church, but God blesses His children also in every place, because He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

134.2.7.en: May you take care of your prayer every night, to declare your love for God, and to thank Him for His care for you all day long, and to offer repentance for your sins, and to ask for quiet sleep in His hands, so that you wake for praise and prayers. Praising the mighty, blessed God. “Alleluia. Praise the name of the LORD; praise Him, O you servants of the LORD) “... v. 1. Introduction:

134.2.8.en: 1- Its writer: unknown; it is one of the orphan psalms whose title does not mention the name of its writer. But some incline to the view that the writer is the prophet David.

134.2.9.en: 2- This psalm calls to the praise of God, and suits everyone who loves God and grows spiritually. We should enjoy being in His hands, and thank Him for His works with us. Therefore this psalm calls to praise three times at its beginning (vv. 1-3) and to blessing God four times at its end (vv. 19-21).

134.2.10.en: 3- This psalm resembles the one before it in praising God, but it is distinguished in that it gives the motives of this praise, which are God's works with His children and the weakness and baseness of the worship of idols. It clearly declares the rejection of pagan worship, and the praise of God alone.

134.2.11.en: 4- This psalm is considered one of the great Hallel psalms that praise and glorify God, together with the psalm after it. The two were chanted in the morning service on the Sabbath and at the feast of the Passover. It is therefore a liturgical psalm. It was also chanted after the return from captivity, and also during the captivity, so that the believers might reject the worship of idols.

134.2.12.en: 5- This psalm begins with the word “Alleluia” and also ends with it, like Psalms (106, 113, 146, 148, 149, 150).

134.2.13.en: 6- This psalm is similar to the ninth chapter of the Book of Nehemiah in that both call the Levites to bless God and thank Him for His great works with His people.

134.2.14.en: 7- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.

135.0.0.en: Alleluia. Praise the name of the LORD; praise Him, O you servants of the LORD.

135.0.1.en: 1- The writer of the psalm calls the servants of the Lord to praise Him, since he has experienced the sweetness of praise; therefore he wants all who believe in God to enjoy praising Him. The sign that declares the faith of the servants of the Lord in Him is that they love Him, and feel His grace, and so thank Him and praise Him.

135.0.2.en: 2- If the servants of the Lord lift their hearts in praise to God, they cling to Him, and God gives them the grace of sonship, which was clearly declared in the New Testament; for Christ, the Only Son in essence, by His redemption of us became the firstborn among many brethren, so we became sons of God, attached to Him, striving to praise Him, like the angels who praise Him at all times; indeed some people have consecrated their lives to praising His holy name, and they are the monastic fathers.

135.0.3.en: 3- Praising the name of the Lord means His person, and this contains all the beauty of the Lord, of virtues and blessings, which His children see and experience.

135.1.0.en: You that stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God.

135.1.1.en: 1- Here the writer of the psalm calls those who stand in the house of the Lord, who are all the believers who offer worship in the house of the Lord, and especially the priests and Levites who stand for long periods to offer worship and prayers and praise to the Lord.

135.1.2.en: 2- “Those who stand” means spiritual vigilance and attention, and it also means reverence in the presence of the great God. It likewise means uprightness in faith before God. All this draws the hearts of God's children to live with Him in holy worship in His temple, and therefore keeps them entirely away from the temples of idols.

135.2.0.en: Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; sing praises unto His name, for it is pleasant.

135.2.1.en: 1- The writer of the psalm, who has experienced the sweetness of praise, calls the priests and Levites to praise God, and what encourages them to praise is that He is good. And whoever comes forward to praise the good God ought to be striving in the way of goodness.

135.2.2.en: 2- When the believers praise the good God, they praise Him for His goodness; He treats them according to His goodness and blesses them. And they praise Him also not only for the benefit and the answer to their requests, but because He is sweet and worthy of praise.

135.3.0.en: For the LORD has chosen Jacob unto Himself, and Israel for His own possession.

135.3.1.en: 1- God chose Jacob, or Israel, the father of the tribes, and all the people of the children of Israel, because of his faith, and his pursuit of the way of perfection, and his love for God, so He shepherded him and cared for him, that this people might be a light to the world and an example to the rest of the peoples; and as God is glorified in His people, He calls the rest of the peoples to believe in Him.

135.3.2.en: 2- God's choice of His people is a great pride that makes this people distinct from the rest of the peoples, as the Law declared (Deut 7:6). And it calls the people to hold fast to the Law and the commandments, that they may enjoy the fellowship of God and His increasing work in them. And all the more in the New Testament, the Christians in the Church are distinguished by God's choice of them, and this makes them hold fast to His word, and unite with Him through the Holy Sacraments, and acquire His virtues, and so enjoy His constant presence with them.

135.3.3.en: God is sweet, and therefore it is natural for us to praise Him, and it is unnatural for us to neglect praising Him; for praise expresses our faith in Him, and our love for Him, and our appreciation of His gifts, for which we thank Him. Therefore may we take care to set aside a time, even if small, every day for praise.

135.4.s.en: (2) The power of ... with His people

135.4.0.en: For I know that the LORD is great, and that our Lord is above all gods. Whatsoever the LORD pleased, that did He in heaven, and in earth, in the seas, and all deep places. He causes the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; He makes lightnings for the rain; He brings the wind out of His treasuries.

135.4.2.en: 1- The writer of the psalm declares his experience with God, and says that He is great, indeed greater than all the pagan gods that the peoples of the world follow. And that He is able to do everything in every place, whether in heaven, or on earth, or in the sea; because He is the Creator of all, and therefore He alone is worthy of prayer, glorification and worship.

135.4.3.en: 2- The writer of the psalm gives examples of God's power: He alone is the One who makes the clouds ascend from the end of the earth to its end. And it is laden with many good things, which are the rains that He pours out on people in God's wisdom in the suitable measure. And He gives light to the sky, which is the lightnings, and likewise He moves the winds in their various directions. These examples signify God's power that sends the Apostles and priests and servants into the world to pour out on it the blessings of God's word and His sacraments, and they are the clouds. As for the lightnings, they signify the spiritual enlightenment that God gives His children. And the winds signify the manifold work of the Holy Spirit in every direction to meet the needs of the Church and the believers.

135.5.0.en: Who smote the firstborn of Egypt, both of man and beast. Who sent tokens and wonders into the midst of you, O Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his servants.

135.5.1.en: 1- God struck the Egyptians with ten plagues to show them the weakness of their gods whom they worshiped, so that they would take heed and return to Him and know that He is the one God.

135.5.2.en: 2- The plagues were gradual so that they might return to Him, but because of the hardness of their hearts the force of the plagues increased until it reached the tenth plague, which is the hardest, in which the firstborn of men were struck, and also the beasts; for the beasts are a blessing from God, so if man deviates God withdraws His gift from him.

135.5.3.en: 3- All these plagues came upon the Egyptians, and did not come upon the children of Israel, for they lived in peace and divine blessings; all this so that the Egyptians would take heed and know the power of God, who shepherds His people and protects them, that perhaps they would believe, and repent, and return to Him.

135.6.0.en: Who smote great nations, and slew mighty kings: Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan; and gave their land for an heritage, an heritage unto Israel His people.

135.6.1.en: 1- After the liberation of the people of God from the slavery of Egypt, and their crossing the wilderness of Sinai, they reached the land of Canaan, and faced at its front, east of the Jordan River, strong peoples of giants, who are the Amorites, headed by Sihon, who signifies pride and haughtiness, and Og, who signifies reliance on blessings and material strength. The children of Israel killed them by the power of God, and crossed the Jordan River, and also triumphed by the power of God over all the kings and kingdoms they faced in the land of Canaan, and possessed their land.

135.6.2.en: 2- The children of Israel triumphed by the power of God over the Canaanite peoples, and killed them because of their evil, and they signify the demons, because they are wicked and worship idols, and they possessed their land in their place; because the people of God believe in Him and walk by His commandments and His Law. And if the people of God go away and walk in evil, God disciplines them with afflictions and captivity. And the cause of all the blessings is faith in God, and walking by His commandments.

135.6.3.en: The power of God with you protects you and reassures you, and even fills your heart with joy as long as you strive in the way of His commandments, and repent if you sin; but beware of negligence lest God abandon you and you suffer many troubles and lose your eternal place.

135.7.s.en: (3) The blessed ... and the corruption of the idols

135.7.0.en: Your name, O LORD, endures for ever; Your memorial, O LORD, throughout all generations.

135.7.1.en: God is eternal and everlasting, so He is different from all the weak pagan gods, and because of His great works with His people, they ought to remember Him and thank Him. This establishes their faith, and develops their love for Him, and then He gives them new blessings, and they live always in joy, reassured, because their God is strong and firm for ever, not only in this generation, that is, the lifetime they spend on the earth, but also in the coming generation, which is eternal life.

135.8.0.en: For the LORD will judge His people, and He will have compassion on His servants.

135.8.1.en: 1- God judges the wicked of His people for their sins, since He is just, and disciplines them that they may return to Him. But if they repent He has compassion on them, and blesses them and compensates them for what is past, as He disciplined His people in the captivity, then supported them and blessed them and brought them back from the captivity.

135.8.2.en: 2- God judges the wicked of His people that they may repent, and has compassion on His servants who believe in Him and keep His commandments, and keeps them from all evil.

135.9.0.en: The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not; eyes have they, but they

135.9.1.en: see not; they have ears, but they hear not; neither is there any breath in their mouths. They that make them are like unto them, and so is every one that trusts in them.

135.9.2.en: These verses are found in (Ps 115:4-6, 8), and this psalm is in this same book, and they have already been explained, so may the reader refer to them. In summary of the explanation, the idols, that is, the pagan gods, are statues made by people with their hands, and they are unable to speak or see or hear or breathe; they are lifeless statues in the form of a man or an animal, and they are cursed and a dwelling for demons, and likewise their makers are wicked, cursed, and tools in the hand of Satan, that is, they lack the ability to speak and see ... what is meant is spiritual speech and insight; their makers are alive in body, dead in spirit, and have no eternal life.

135.10.0.en: Bless the LORD, O house of Israel; bless the LORD, O house of Aaron; bless the LORD, O house of Levi; you that fear the LORD, bless the LORD.

135.10.1.en: 1- The psalm closes with a call to bless the Lord and glorify Him, calling first all the people of God, then the priests, the leaders of the service, and after them the Levites, the servants of the temple, and finally those who fear the Lord, that is, the righteous and the just; so all the classes of the people praise God.

135.10.2.en: 2- He mentions these different classes, and calls them to praise, because each class differs from the other in praising God, and God in His love accepts all spiritual levels. In addition, He singles out the priests and Levites because they are an example to the people. As for those who fear the Lord, it is a call to them to increase their praise and blessing of God, since they have loved righteousness and godliness.

135.10.3.en: 3- There is a resemblance between these two verses and Psalm 115 (vv. 9-11); in Psalm 115 He calls these classes to trust in God, and here He calls them to bless God. These two verses also resemble Psalm 118 (vv. 2-4), in which He calls them to thank God.

135.11.0.en: Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, who dwells at Jerusalem. Alleluia.

135.11.1.en: 1- God is blessed from Zion, that is, from His holy temple, for from the temple many praises ascend, more than ascend in the houses of the believers. And those who enter the temple express their blessing of God by offering many sacrifices and prayers.

135.11.2.en: 2- God is blessed in the midst of His people Israel, because He dwells among them. And this moves the hearts of all the people to reassurance and joy and pride, and finally praise; indeed it is a call to constant praise, because God dwells always in their midst. And he expresses this praise when he ends the psalm with the word Alleluia.

135.11.3.en: God dwells in your heart because you receive His Body and Blood, indeed He is united with you; does this not call you to glorify Him and to constant prayers to God from your heart and your tongue, whether by repeating the psalms or the hymns, or the Jesus Prayer?

135.11.5.en: “Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His mercy endures for ever” (v. 1). Introduction:

135.11.6.en: 1- Its writer: unknown; it is one of the orphan psalms, that is, those whose writer's name is not known in their title. But there is an opinion that its writer is David, on the evidence that he said of God, “for His mercy endures for ever,” when he moved the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr 16:41). Then his son Solomon repeated it after him at the dedication of the temple (2 Chr 5:13). And after them Ezra prayed it on the day of the rebuilding of the second temple (Ezra 3:11).

135.11.7.en: 2- This psalm is one of the most important psalms of thanksgiving to God and is called the Great Hallel, that is, the great rejoicing, together with its companion, the previous psalm.

135.11.8.en: 3- This psalm is liturgical; it was chanted daily in the praise of God, in addition to the New Year and the feast of the Passover.

135.11.9.en: 4- The manner of repeating this psalm was in different forms:

135.11.11.en: b- One group repeats the first part of every quarter (verse), which is the part whose words differ from the other quarters, and the other group repeats the repeated part, which is “Alleluia, for His mercy endures for ever.”

135.11.12.en: c- One chanter says the different part of the verse, and the company of chanters repeats the repeated part.

135.11.13.en: 5- This psalm suits everyone who loves God and wishes to praise Him and glorify Him, so he stands firm in his faith, and his joy increases, and even his delight in life.

135.11.14.en: 6- This psalm is repeated in the Church daily and is called the Second Hos, that is, the Second Praise.

135.11.15.en: 7- This psalm was chanted in the Old Testament and also in the early Church; the history of the Church in the fourth century tells us that Pope Athanasius the Apostolic was in the church chanting this psalm with the people when soldiers attacked to arrest him by order of the king, and in his calm he signaled to all to continue the praise in their loud voice, so the soldiers stopped before this powerful celebration, and he withdrew quietly through the back doors, and they could not arrest him.

135.11.16.en: 8- The repetition of the last part of every verse 26 times in this psalm is not a vain repetition, but is because of:

135.11.17.en: a- The greatness of God's mercy, which has no limit, and the mind cannot grasp its extent.

135.11.18.en: b- To establish in the heart thanksgiving to God for His mercies, so that man's attachment to God increases.

135.11.19.en: c- To repel all the attacks of the devil with doubt and murmuring.

135.11.20.en: 9- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.
